summary: Today’s pulse tracks Poundland owner extracted millions when chain was on ‘knife-edge’, MPs say, Double amputee marathon runner criticises Badenoch for ‘weaponising his success’, and British soldier charged with rape of army servicewoman in Cyprus. Across Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are charged, claims, and hegseth. In the background, Trump praises Hegseth after failed impeachment effort and shrugs off Iran war criticism - live and Ex-member of radical Marxist group scales balcony, escapes house arrest in Argentina keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Poundland owner extracted millions when chain was on ‘knife-edge’, MPs say
headlines.description: Retailer’s management to seek two-week extension of legal protection from creditors in high court MPs have accused the owner of Poundland of extracting millions of pounds from the budget retailer when it was on a “knife-edge” as it seeks extra time to secure a rescue deal. The management of Poundland, which employs 12,000 people and operates 600 stores in the UK and Ireland, will seek a two-week extension of legal protection from creditors from the high court on Thursday morning.

headlines.title: Double amputee marathon runner criticises Badenoch for ‘weaponising his success’
headlines.description: Paralympian Richard Whitehead ‘gobsmacked’ at Tory leader’s speech over proposed £36bn welfare cuts The double amputee marathon runner Richard Whitehead has criticised Kemi Badenoch for “weaponising his sporting success” to justify her proposed £36bn welfare cuts. The Conservative leader used the example of “ double amputees running marathons ” in a speech this week to explain the reasoning behind her proposed cuts to disability benefits, which she said were enabling people to “live a life of dependency”.

headlines.title: British soldier charged with rape of army servicewoman in Cyprus
headlines.description: L/Cpl Nicholas Horne, from 4th Battalion of Royal Regiment of Scotland, charged with one count of rape on 23 October A British soldier has been charged with the alleged rape of a UK army servicewoman in Cyprus. L/Cpl Nicholas Horne, who serves in the 4th Battalion of the Royal Regiment of Scotland , also known as The Highlanders, was charged with one count of rape on 23 October, the Defence Serious Crime Command (DSCC) said.

headlines.title: Trump praises Hegseth after failed impeachment effort and shrugs off Iran war criticism - live
headlines.description: President claims US ‘did not start war with Iran’ in Veterans Day speech where he also backed defense secretary again day after failed impeachment vote Democrats lambast absent peers over failed Hegseth impeachment House Republicans block effort to impeach Hegseth By a vote of 211-204, Republicans referred the articles of impeachment to the judiciary committee – effectively killing the effort to oust Hegseth.

headlines.title: Ex-member of radical Marxist group scales balcony, escapes house arrest in Argentina
headlines.description: 74-year-old Leonardo Bertulazzi, awaiting extradition to Italy, reportedly used harness to flee custody A 74-year-old former member of Italy ’s radical Marxist group the Red Brigades has escaped from house arrest in Argentina , the country’s security ministry confirmed on Wednesday. Authorities placed Leonardo Bertulazzi under house arrest in Buenos Aires in 2024, prior to his extradition to Italy to serve a 27-year prison sentence.

headlines.title: Complaint filed to IRS in relation to Fifa head Gianni Infantino’s housekeeper
headlines.description: It calls for inquiry into claims she was on Fifa payroll Fifa: Infantino personally pays for ‘any domestic staff’ A complaint has been filed to the United States Internal Revenue Service calling for an investigation into claims an individual on the Fifa payroll was working privately as a housekeeper for Gianni Infantino. If the IRS investigates and finds the claims to be proven then Fifa could lose its tax-exempt status in the US. Fifa has 501(c)(4) status in the country, a category for organisations “created to promote community welfare for charitable, educational or recreational purposes”.

headlinePool.title: ‘The world we know is over’ without urgent climate action, leaders tell Cop31
headlinePool.description: Marshall Islands president warns of worsening floods as UN chief calls for a windfall tax on oil and gas firms Failure to provide an overwhelming response to the climate crisis means “the world we know is over”, the president of the embattled Marshall Islands has warned, as dozens of leaders gathered in Turkey for the Cop31 climate summit. Hilda Heine, one of a handful of Pacific Island leaders to make an impassioned speech at Cop31 on Wednesday, told other heads of state that overshooting the 1.5C Paris temperature target would mean waves eating away their shores and floods that destroy towns, schools and hospitals.

headlinePool.title: Millions join Spain’s first general strike in 14 years in protest at housing costs
headlinePool.description: Twenty-four-hour stoppage draws high participation weeks before election in which far right could gain power Millions of people across Spain have joined the country’s first general strike in 14 years, setting up picket lines to protest against soaring housing prices before an election in which the far right could be catapulted into power. At the centre of Wednesday’s nationwide 24-hour stoppage, singularly called for by tenants’ associations and later backed by workers’ unions, is a pushback against Spain’s deepening housing crisis.

headlinePool.title: Trump planning new military assault or tighter sanctions, say Iranian officials
headlinePool.description: Regime adviser says Tehran could be forced into pre-emptive strikes if stalemate continues Senior Iranian officials believe the US is planning either further military strikes or an ever-tightening economic stranglehold that will push Tehran into retaliatory action. The assessment comes from Mehdi Mohammadi, an adviser to Iran’s chief negotiator in talks with the US, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf.

headlinePool.title: Schools in Italy, Scotland and Northern Ireland hit by threats in suspected bomb hoax
headlinePool.description: More than 6,000 Italian schools received a threat. Authorities in all three countries say there appears to be no risk to the public. It is not known if the incidents are linked.

headlinePool.title: US Coast Guard suspends search for woman swept out to sea in California
headlinePool.description: Senah Park, 24, was last seen near Panther state beach on Sunday evening amid historic high tides and water levels The US Coast Guard announced that it has suspended its search for a 24-year-old woman who is believed to have been swept out to sea in California . The woman, identified as 24-year-old Senah Park, was last seen near Panther state beach in Santa Cruz county at about 8.30pm local time on Sunday, authorities said earlier this week.

headlinePool.title: Burnham raised safety concerns about Manchester ‘monster’ warehouse, inquiry hears
headlinePool.description: PM wrote to transport commissioner to oppose ‘megashed’ in Astley shortly before he entered No 10 Andy Burnham raised safety concerns about dozens of lorries leaving a “monster” warehouse near a primary school because there was “no safe crossing” for children, a public inquiry has heard. Concerns about the 18-metre-high “megashed” in the village of Astley , Greater Manchester, are being examined by Britain’s office of the transport commissioner.

headlinePool.title: ITV to cut show budgets as UK TV and film production spend drops by more than £2bn
headlinePool.description: Broadcaster plans to make £30m in ‘temporary’ savings before inquiry into takeover by Sky Business live – latest updates ITV plans to slash its programming budget as new figures showed that spend on the production of films and prestige TV shows in the UK was down more than £2bn over the last year. The broadcaster plans to make £30m in “temporary” savings, including £25m in content and £5m elsewhere in the business.

headlinePool.title: Democrats lambast absent peers allowing Republicans to squash Hegseth impeachment attempt
headlinePool.description: Eleven Democrats missed the key procedural vote on the impeachment effort, which failed by just seven votes US politics live – latest updates Democratic lawmakers expressed outrage at nearly a dozen of their colleagues for missing a vote Tuesday evening to impeach the defense secretary, Pete Hegseth , allowing Republicans to squash the effort. Eleven Democrats missed the key procedural vote on the impeachment effort , which failed by just seven votes. Some blamed traffic and conflicting events and others accused Speaker Mike Johnson of closing the vote early. Many of those not in the Capitol said they support the effort to impeach Hegseth.

headlinePool.title: Missing 11-month-old baby found buried alive in a crate in South Carolina
headlinePool.description: Officials say the child was found close to his father's home on Tuesday, a day after he was taken, and is being cared for in hospital.
